text: I run a small UK business that gets paid, and pays suppliers, through PayPal. So I built Accnomos to keep those books.

Accnomos keeps the books in your own OneDrive or Google Drive, and files VAT to HMRC. Press Sync PayPal, and it fetches every payment from PayPal itself: the gross, PayPal's fee and the net, matched to the invoice it pays. A sale with no invoice waits for me to choose its VAT. Nothing posts until I approve.

text: Then I just ask. What did PayPal cost me this quarter? How much is in PayPal? The answers come from those PayPal entries, worked out by code to the penny, and explained in plain English.
And the tie-out checks the books against PayPal's own balance, shows when PayPal last refreshed it, and explains any difference.

Paying a supplier works the other way. When a bill falls due, Accnomos offers to pay it by PayPal payout. I approve, PayPal confirms in about half a minute, and only then does it post. A retry can never pay twice. PayPal can't date a payout ahead, so it goes on the due date, when the app is open.
If a customer opens a dispute, Accnomos builds the evidence pack from the books, checks every figure by code, and waits for me to read it before anything goes to PayPal.
The AI fetches and explains. Code calculates. I approve.

And PayPal sits inside a full set of books. Scan a receipt and approve it. Match the bank. Send invoices and quotes. Work out VAT and file it to HMRC's sandbox. Run reports. Ask by typing or by voice. Track jobs, mileage and payroll estimates. Plan the day around your calendar. Keep your contacts. The books stay in your own drive, on the web and on Android, with guides built in, and upcoming PayPal payments go straight into your calendar.
